headline: Clinton order sets up an advisory commission on consumer protection and quality in the health care industry.
what_it_does: This order creates an advisory commission focused on consumer protection and quality of care in the health care industry. Based on its title, the commission's role is to study these issues and give advice. An advisory commission like this usually makes recommendations and does not set binding rules by itself. No summary was provided, so further details are not available here.

who_it_affects.group: Patients and people who use health care services
who_it_affects.how: They are the focus of the commission's work on consumer protection and quality, though advice alone does not change their rights or costs.

who_it_affects.group: Health care industry, such as health plans and providers
who_it_affects.how: Their practices are the subject of the commission's review and possible recommendations.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed September 5, 1996; executive orders usually take effect when signed.
